<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.Ex6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=v_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=v_{s}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS2.p5.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS2.p5.2.1" class="ltx_text">The transition from conditioning on <math id="S3.SS2.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>q</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S3.SS2.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> follows because the samples <math id="S3.SS2.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> are chosen according to the same distribution as <math id="S3.SS2.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p6" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS2.p6.1" class="ltx_p">Theorem <a href="#Thmtheorem2" title="Theorem 2. ‣ 3.2 𝑃(𝑠,𝑀): generality of 𝑠 ‣ 3 Our Metric: Prior-Aware (PA) Memorization ‣ Prior Aware Memorization: An Efficient Metric for Distinguishing Memorization from Generalization in Large Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> shows that <math id="S3.SS2.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Var[\hat{v_{s}}]\rightarrow 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>V</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mover accent="true"><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>^</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Var[\hat{v_{s}}]\rightarrow 0</annotation></semantics></math> as <math id="S3.SS2.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c\rightarrow\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c\rightarrow\infty</annotation></semantics></math>. This means that over a large number of prefixes sampled from the dataset, the error of the estimator tends to <math id="S3.SS2.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math> for Theorem <a href="#Thmtheorem2" title="Theorem 2. ‣ 3.2 𝑃(𝑠,𝑀): generality of 𝑠 ‣ 3 Our Metric: Prior-Aware (PA) Memorization ‣ Prior Aware Memorization: An Efficient Metric for Distinguishing Memorization from Generalization in Large Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>. We state the theorem below, but relegate its proof to Appendix <a href="#A1" title="Appendix A Proof for Theorem ‣ Prior Aware Memorization: An Efficient Metric for Distinguishing Memorization from Generalization in Large Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A</span></a> due to space constraints.</p>
</div>
<div id="Thmtheorem2" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_theorem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmtheorem2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem 2</span></span><span id="Thmtheorem2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmtheorem2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmtheorem2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="Thmtheorem2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Var[\hat{v_{s}}]=\frac{1}{c}\cdot Var[P(s\mid p_{i})]\leq\frac{1}{4c}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>V</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mover accent="true"><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>^</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>c</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mi>V</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Var[\hat{v_{s}}]=\frac{1}{c}\cdot Var[P(s\mid p_{i})]\leq\frac{1}{4c}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="Thmtheorem2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text"></span></p>
</div>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">4 </span>Evaluation</h2>

<div id="S4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this section, we empirically evaluate whether Prior Aware Memorization correlates with Counterfactual Memorization, another metric that aims to distinguish memorization from generalization. We perform <math id="S4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math> small scale experiments to verify this correlation, one with synthetic data, and one with real data. Finally, we evaluate PA memorization on a large scale with pre-trained models and note any trends.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.1 </span>Correlation with Counterfactual Memorization</h3>

<div id="S4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this section, we empirically show that PA memorization does indeed filter out <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\|s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo fence="false">|</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\|s</annotation></semantics></math> where <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math> is statistically popular by correlating it with counterfactual memorization <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang et al. (2023)</a></cite>, another metric that can measure statistically likely sequences. To do so, we train several models in a controlled setting, and measure both counterfactual memorization and <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{P(s\mid p)}{\hat{v}_{s}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mfrac><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>v</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>s</mi></msub></mfrac><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{P(s\mid p)}{\hat{v}_{s}}</annotation></semantics></math>. We then show that these are positively correlated.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS1.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">4.1.1 </span>Counterfactual Memorization</h4>

<div id="S4.SS1.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Below, we restate the definition of Counterfactual memorization from <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang et al. (2023)</a></cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="Thmdefinition4" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_definition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmdefinition4.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Definition 4</span></span><span id="Thmdefinition4.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Counterfactual Memorization)<span id="Thmdefinition4.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmdefinition4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="Thmdefinition4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmdefinition4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Given a training algorithm <math id="Thmdefinition4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>A</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A</annotation></semantics></math> that maps a training
dataset <math id="Thmdefinition4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>D</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D</annotation></semantics></math> to a trained model <math id="Thmdefinition4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>f</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math>, and a measure <math id="Thmdefinition4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L(f,x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>f</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L(f,x)</annotation></semantics></math> of the accuracy of <math id="Thmdefinition4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>f</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> on a specific example
<math id="Thmdefinition4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>, the counterfactual memorization of a training example <math id="Thmdefinition4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> in <math id="Thmdefinition4.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>D</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D</annotation></semantics></math> is given by</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.SSS1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<table id="S4.EGx3" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S4.E5"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S4.E5.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\displaystyle\text{mem}(x)\triangleq\underset{\scriptscriptstyle S\subset D,x\in S}{E}[L(A(S),x)]-\underset{\scriptscriptstyle S\prime\subset D,x\notin S\prime}{E}[L(A(S\prime),x)]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext>mem</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>≜</mo><munder accentunder="true"><mi>E</mi><mrow><mrow><mi mathsize="0.500em">S</mi><mo mathsize="0.500em">⊂</mo><mi mathsize="0.500em">D</mi></mrow><mo mathsize="0.500em">,</mo><mrow><mi mathsize="0.500em">x</mi><mo mathsize="0.500em">∈</mo><mi mathsize="0.500em">S</mi></mrow></mrow></munder><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>L</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>A</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>S</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><munder accentunder="true"><mi>E</mi><mrow><mi mathsize="0.500em">S</mi><mo lspace="0em" mathsize="0.500em" rspace="0.1389em">′</mo><mo lspace="0.1389em" mathsize="0.500em">⊂</mo><mi mathsize="0.500em">D</mi><mo mathsize="0.500em">,</mo><mi mathsize="0.500em">x</mi><mo mathsize="0.500em">∉</mo><mi mathsize="0.500em">S</mi><mo lspace="0em" mathsize="0.500em">′</mo></mrow></munder><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>L</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>A</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>S</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">′</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\text{mem}(x)\triangleq\underset{\scriptscriptstyle S\subset D,x\in S}{E}[L(A(S),x)]-\underset{\scriptscriptstyle S\prime\subset D,x\notin S\prime}{E}[L(A(S\prime),x)]</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(5)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S4.SS1.SSS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS1.SSS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="S\prime" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo lspace="0em">′</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S\prime</annotation></semantics></math>
are subsets of training examples sampled from <math id="S4.SS1.SSS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>D</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D</annotation></semantics></math>. The expectation is taken with
respect to the random sampling of <math id="S4.SS1.SSS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS1.SSS1.p2.m5" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="S\prime" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo lspace="0em">′</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S\prime</annotation></semantics></math>, as well as the randomness in the training algorithm <math id="S4.SS1.SSS1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>A</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A</annotation></semantics></math>. Generally speaking, the first term measures the expected accuracy over models that contain the target sequence <math id="S4.SS1.SSS1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>, and the second measures the same over models that do not contain <math id="S4.SS1.SSS1.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS1.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">4.1.2 </span>Metric measurements.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS1.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We describe how we measure Equations (<a href="#S4.E5" title="In 4.1.1 Counterfactual Memorization ‣ 4.1 Correlation with Counterfactual Memorization ‣ 4 Evaluation ‣ Prior Aware Memorization: An Efficient Metric for Distinguishing Memorization from Generalization in Large Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>) and (<a href="#Thmdefinition2" title="Definition 2 (Prior-Aware memorization). ‣ 3 Our Metric: Prior-Aware (PA) Memorization ‣ Prior Aware Memorization: An Efficient Metric for Distinguishing Memorization from Generalization in Large Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>) in our experiments.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.SSS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS1.SSS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Counterfactual Memorization.</span> In our setup, we interpret <math id="S4.SS1.SSS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> in  (<a href="#S4.E5" title="In 4.1.1 Counterfactual Memorization ‣ 4.1 Correlation with Counterfactual Memorization ‣ 4 Evaluation ‣ Prior Aware Memorization: An Efficient Metric for Distinguishing Memorization from Generalization in Large Language Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>) as <math id="S4.SS1.SSS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\|s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo fence="false">|</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\|s</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="S4.SS1.SSS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS1.SSS2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math> are of equal length. To simplify notation, we use <math id="S4.SS1.SSS2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS1.SSS2.p2.m6" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="M\prime" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0em">′</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M\prime</annotation></semantics></math> to refer to <math id="S4.SS1.SSS2.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A(S)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>S</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A(S)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS1.SSS2.p2.m8" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="A(S\prime)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>S</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">′</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A(S\prime)</annotation></semantics></math> respectively, which we refer to as the target (<math id="S4.SS1.SSS2.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>) and baseline (<math id="S4.SS1.SSS2.p2.m10" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="M\prime" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0em">′</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M\prime</annotation></semantics></math>) models (described below). To measure the accuracy of the model <math id="S4.SS1.SSS2.p2.m11" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="M(x=p\|s)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M(x=p\|s)</annotation></semantics></math>, we utilize the measure <math id="S4.SS1.SSS2.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\log(P(s\mid p;M))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>;</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\log(P(s\mid p;M))</annotation></semantics></math>, following the definition of extractable memorization presented in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">Carlini et al. (2022)</a></cite>. The expectation is taken over all models trained with the same ratio of near-duplicates to exact copies.
As in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang et al. (2023)</a></cite>, we assume these models are uniformly distributed, so the expectation reduces to the average of <math id="S4.SS1.SSS2.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\log(P(s\mid p))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\log(P(s\mid p))</annotation></semantics></math> across multiple trained models. Thus, we measure the following:</p>
<table id="S4.EGx4" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S4.E6"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S4.E6.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\displaystyle E_{M}[\log(P(s\mid p;M))]-E_{M\prime}[\log(P(s\mid p;M\prime))]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>E</mi><mi>M</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>log</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>P</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>;</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>E</mi><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0em">′</mo></mrow></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>log</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>P</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>;</mo><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">′</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle E_{M}[\log(P(s\mid p;M))]-E_{M\prime}[\log(P(s\mid p;M\prime))]</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(6)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS2.p2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS1.SSS2.p2.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">PA Memorization.</span> To keep PA memorization comparable with counterfactual memorization, instead of measuring <math id="S4.SS1.SSS2.p2.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="E_{M}[\frac{P(s\mid p;M)}{\hat{v}_{s;M}}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>E</mi><mi>M</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>;</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>v</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>;</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow></msub></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E_{M}[\frac{P(s\mid p;M)}{\hat{v}_{s;M}}]</annotation></semantics></math>, we measure its log, like so:</p>
<table id="S4.EGx5" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S4.E7"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S4.E7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle E_{M}[\log(\frac{P(s\mid p;M)}{\hat{v}_{s}})]=E_{M}[\log(P(s\mid p;M))]-E_{M}[\log(\hat{v}_{s;M})]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>E</mi><mi>M</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>;</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>v</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>s</mi></msub></mfrac></mstyle><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>E</mi><mi>M</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>;</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>E</mi><mi>M</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>v</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>;</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle E_{M}[\log(\frac{P(s\mid p;M)}{\hat{v}_{s}})]=E_{M}[\log(P(s\mid p;M))]-E_{M}[\log(\hat{v}_{s;M})]</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
